page.title: Trade
page.lead: Restaurants, wine bars, wine shops and delis across the UK and Northern Europe buy from Lento at trade prices, in mixed cases, with VAT handled for their country.

prices.body: Once approved, every price on the site switches to trade, excluding VAT, with the retail price shown alongside.

vat.title: VAT
vat.body: Italy: 22% Italian VAT. EU: intra-Community supply with reverse charge (0%). UK and Norway: export, 0% VAT; import VAT and duties are settled at destination.

orders.title: Order requests
orders.body: No payment online: you send an order request, we confirm availability and send a pro-forma invoice. Payment by bank transfer, 30 days for established accounts.

delivery.title: Delivery
delivery.body: We ship from a bonded warehouse in Italy under excise suspension where applicable. Delivery is quoted on the pro-forma; free from 60 bottles.

intro.all: Everything here was made slowly, by someone whose name we know: wines from small Italian growers, and foods from the families who refused to let them disappear.
intro.wine: Wine as it used to be made: grapes picked by hand, yeasts from the vineyard, years in old casks. Bottles that taste of a hill, a season and a family — not of a recipe.
intro.new: Just arrived from Italy: the bottles and jars we fell for on our latest visits, from growers we go back to every year.
intro.orange: White grapes left on their skins, as farmers along Italy's borders always did. Amber, savoury and alive, with a grip that asks for food and good company.
intro.white: Whites from old pergolas and volcanic slopes, made without make-up: salt, herbs and light, and the quiet confidence of a place.
intro.red: Reds made with patience, in old wood and clay, by growers who would rather wait a year than hurry a wine. To be poured at a long table and remembered.
intro.sparkling: Refermented in the bottle, the farmhouse way: cloudy, dry and alive, just as it was drunk at home.
intro.pantry: The Italian kitchen begins here. Anchovies, beans, olives, honey and cheese made in small batches by the people who grow, fish and age them — the flavours a grandmother would recognise.
intro.treasures: Foods made in a few tonnes a year and kept alive by a handful of families. Every jar you open is a reason for them to make it again next year.

producers.title: Producers
producers.description: We work with a few families and cooperatives we know personally: growers who farm by hand, and the keepers of rare traditional foods — our Italian Food Treasures.
producers.partnersBody: Small producers who keep a traditional food alive, made the slow way and sold at a fair price.

stories.title: Stories
stories.description: Where our wines and foods come from, and the people who make them.

hero.title: Wines that take their time.
hero.alt: A vineyard in the late afternoon
hero.lead: Lento means slow. We bring wines from Italian growers who take their time, and rare traditional foods — our Italian Food Treasures — to tables in the UK and Northern Europe.

growers.title: Small growers
growers.body: Families farming a few hectares organically, by hand, in places they know stone by stone.

cellar.title: Made as it used to be
cellar.body: Native yeasts, long fermentations, old casks or amphorae: wines that taste of a place, not of the cellar.

treasures.title: Foods worth saving
treasures.body: Traditional foods made in tiny quantities, bought directly at the price their makers set.

treasures.title: The pantry
treasures.body: Colatura from Cetara, anchovies caught with the menaica net, chickpeas from Cicerale, a cheese aged in amphorae: foods made in tiny quantities by people who refused to let them disappear.

marquee.label: What Lento stands for
marquee.first: Natural wine doesn't exist*|Good wine will always triumph over evil|In vino veritas — in ours, a little sediment too|A la volè!|Cloudy is the new clear|Slow, except at dinner
